title: Under the celestial arch
caption: The arc of the Milky Way over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The bright arc of the Milky Way spans the sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory. On the ground stand two instruments. On the right stands ESO's 3.6-metre optical telescope in its dome, and on the left the silvery dish of the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope. That dish was retired in 2003 to make way for APEX and ALMA, yet it still seems to gaze hopefully upward.

Hanging from the top of the arc is a bright red feature, the Gum Nebula. Like similar regions along the Milky Way, it is an emission nebula, gas made to glow by radiation from nearby bright stars. Dark filaments of dust break up the band, and inside them new stars are forming that will join the display in the millennia ahead.

Beneath the arc lies the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf galaxy that accompanies our own. Its sibling, the Small Magellanic Cloud, sits below it, just right of the dish. Over on the right, Jupiter shines against the faint gegenschein, a glow that only the darkest skies reveal.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by Petr Horálek. The source does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: Faint features such as the gegenschein and the red glow of the Gum Nebula may show up far more strongly in a camera that gathers light over time than to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: ESO Photo Ambassador Petr Horálek took the image. La Silla ranks among the world's best astronomical sites, known for dark skies and clear air, and a display that most people rarely get to see is an everyday sight at observing sites of its kind.
alt: The Milky Way arching over a telescope dome at right and a dish antenna at left, with a red nebula at the top of the arc, two fuzzy patches below and a bright planet at right.
